basis: Metabolic skeletal myopathy; singleton cytopenia and ophthalmoparesis reports do not establish common involvement across ISCU disease.
Inherited keratoconus causes corneal thinning and ectasia.
Inherited heme-synthesis defect causes sideroblastic anemia; hepatic abnormalities and glucose intolerance are occasional (5-29%).
Adrenal cortisol excess; myopathy/bone loss occurs in roughly 50-80%, skin atrophy/fragility in >50%, and hypertension in about 70% of overt Cushing cases.
Immune myositis; sclerodactyly (30-79%) indicates skin fibrosis. Dysphagia may reflect skeletal-muscle dysfunction; interstitial lung abnormalities are occasional (5-29%).
Disordered growth and osteonecrosis affecting bone growth centers.
Congenital aortic narrowing; associated cardiac abnormalities remain within the cardiovascular axis. Stroke is very rare (1-4%).
Inherited ammonia metabolism disorder; hyperammonemic brain injury and persistent cognitive dysfunction affect approximately 30-60%, varying by subtype and severity.
Papillary inflammation of the conjunctiva; morphology alone does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated cause.
Mosaic schwannomatosis produces nerve-sheath tumors; vestibular or cutaneous involvement is not established as common across this concept.
Defining syndrome features include craniosynostosis, joint contractures and scoliosis, external-ear malformation, and cleft palate.
Structural defect of the iris.
Holoprosencephaly and craniosynostosis define the syndrome; strabismus (80-99%) supports common impairment of ocular alignment and binocular function.
Complement C9 deficiency is an immunodeficiency; susceptibility to invasive infection does not establish damage to another organ.
Mitochondrial metabolic disease defined by hepatic and cerebral involvement; renal disease belongs to a narrower subtype.
Disease localized to the vitreous humor; infection is confined to particular subtypes.
Infiltrative astroglial tumor arising in the central nervous system.
Bone fragility and dysplasia define disease; persistent acanthosis nigricans occurs in 3/5 (60%). Blue sclerae do not impair vision; insulin resistance occurs in 1/5.
Localized mast-cell neoplasm, predominantly arising in skin; hematopoietic lineage and usual cutaneous site define it. Pulmonary tumors are rare extracutaneous forms.
Phenylalanine metabolism defect; untreated PKU causes permanent cognitive injury and represents >30% of this spectrum. Mild hyperphenylalaninemia may spare the brain.
Penile erectile-tissue disorder, outside the organ axes; vascular ancestry alone does not establish vessel disease. Hematologic and spinal causes are separate conditions.
Zellweger-spectrum metabolic disease; brain injury, liver dysfunction and retinal disease are each common (>30%). Common sensorineural hearing loss omitted at the four-axis cap.
Benign neoplasm of uterine endometrial stroma; reproductive organs have no axis. Uterine bleeding alone does not establish hematologic disease.
Spinal neural/meningeal malformation with a stalk and the vertebral closure defect of spina bifida; common additional organ injury is not established.
Immune dysregulation; colitis/parotitis, chronic otitis media and arthritis each occur in 1/2 (50%). Hepatomegaly and glycogen accumulation alone do not establish hepatic injury.
